title: `class:fighter.wind_up`: Wind-up (Breaker rank I)
notes:
- **Mode:** Wick icon, 1024 x 1024 PNG, transparent.
- **Save as:** `art/icons/moves/wind-up.png`.
- **Shows:** Class move card. Wind-up: the Breaker starts each fight with Momentum already stored.
paint: Wick coiled for a heavy swing: weight on a bent back leg, torso twisted away from the target, both hands gripping a long heavy-headed weapon drawn back behind his shoulder with its head high over his back. Two short curved arcs trail behind the weapon head to show the tension stored, not motion blur. The front foot is light, toes forward. The meaning is Momentum already stored before the first blow. At icon size it must read as a figure cocked back with a heavy head over the shoulder. Avoid: the swing already landing, an impact burst, sparks, a spinning blur, a specific named weapon, a spring or a clock, text.
staging: Use one simple block-headed practice maul. One straight continuous haft runs through both separate mitten grips to a single compact blunt head socket. Keep the two visible haft sections on the same line. Over-shoulder wind-up is two-handed and supported by the two grips, never an X, no extra blade or shaft. Shift body weight to back leg.
label: Wind-up (Breaker rank I)
prompt:
Draw one icon in pure white flat ink (#FFFFFF) on a fully transparent background, in exactly the style of the attached reference icons: Wick, the small figure of the trait and perk icons with the ceramic pixel-screen head, capelet and lantern heart, in bold flat white shapes, a confident inked silhouette with a few interior cuts, the same line weight. No outline in another colour, no shading, no gradient, no texture, no glow, no colour and no grey. Wick is the only full figure; anyone else is a partial (a hand, a shoulder, a silhouette cut by the frame). One action, centred, with clear space around it, square, 1024 x 1024 PNG with transparency. It must read at 32 px in a row and at 44 px on a chip: silhouette first, two or three interior cuts at most. No text, no letters, no numbers, no border, no frame. Invented shapes only: nothing recognisable from real-world works, brands, insignia or religions. The icon shows:
Wick coiled for a heavy swing: weight on a bent back leg, torso twisted away from the target, both hands gripping a long heavy-headed weapon drawn back behind his shoulder with its head high over his back. Two short curved arcs trail behind the weapon head to show the tension stored, not motion blur. The front foot is light, toes forward. The meaning is Momentum already stored before the first blow. At icon size it must read as a figure cocked back with a heavy head over the shoulder. Avoid: the swing already landing, an impact burst, sparks, a spinning blur, a specific named weapon, a spring or a clock, text.
Wick always has the exact approved oversized rounded ceramic screen head, transparent face recess with white pixel expression, ear discs, offset shell fittings, short asymmetric capelet, lantern-heart inset, chunky mitten hands and cuffed boots. The silhouette of the head ends at the smooth ceramic shell. There is NO flame, tuft, plume, candle or object attached to or above his head. Resolve any stale flame wording through the angle or pixel expression. Omit default floating cup and reference arrows.
Use one simple block-headed practice maul. One straight continuous haft runs through both separate mitten grips to a single compact blunt head socket. Keep the two visible haft sections on the same line. Over-shoulder wind-up is two-handed and supported by the two grips, never an X, no extra blade or shaft. Shift body weight to back leg. 
All dark voids are physically transparent alpha cutouts, never solid black or gray. Clear border, stable negative space at game size, pure white flat ink.
